annotations.description: The player chose to mulligan a 7-card hand that had 2 Plains, multiple white creatures including a 1-drop (Infantry Veteran), a 2-drop (Daybreak Charger), a combat trick (Moment of Triumph), and powerful late-game cards (Blessed Sanctuary, Knight of the Tusk). While the hand only has 2 lands, both are Plains which cast all the early plays. This is a keepable hand - it has a strong curve if it draws a third land, and even without one it can deploy Infantry Veteran turn 1 and Daybreak Charger turn 2. Mulliganing to 6 loses a card for no good reason.
annotations.actionTaken: Mulliganed a 7-card hand with 2 Plains, a 1-drop, a 2-drop, a combat trick, and strong late-game cards.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has a playable curve starting turn 1 with Infantry Veteran, turn 2 Daybreak Charger, and just needs to draw one more land for the mid-game plays. Two lands with low-curve spells is a reasonable keep.

annotations.description: Playing Forest turn 1 instead of Treetop Village. Since there's nothing to cast turn 1 and Treetop Village enters tapped, playing it now costs nothing while saving a future turn's tempo. The player has no 1-mana plays, so the tapped land is free on turn 1.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest on turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play Treetop Village turn 1 (enters tapped for free since no T1 plays), then Swamp turn 2 for Oathsworn Vampire, Forest turn 3 for Uktabi Orangutan.

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Swamp means GPT5n Perfect cannot cast anything this turn. Playing Swamp would give Forest + Swamp = {1}{B}, allowing Oathsworn Vampire to be cast this turn as a 2/2 creature. Missing a turn of development when the opponent also has limited board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest, leaving no castable spells this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp, then cast Oathsworn Vampire ({1}{B}) to develop the board. Oathsworn Vampire enters tapped so it wouldn't block anyway, but getting it down a turn earlier is meaningful tempo.

annotations.description: Chose Oathsworn Vampire (enters tapped, 2/2) over Uktabi Orangutan (2/2, enters untapped and can block immediately). The remaining 2 mana from casting Vampire has no useful purpose this turn since there's nothing in hand that costs 2 or less. Orangutan's ETB is wasted (no artifacts), but the untapped body is more immediately useful for blocking. Vampire's graveyard recursion is long-term upside, but playing the Orangutan now and saving the Vampire for a turn where its recursion or the tap drawback matters less could be better.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Oathsworn Vampire, leaving 2 mana unused with no way to spend it
annotations.betterLine: Cast Uktabi Orangutan as the 2/2 that enters untapped and can immediately block, saving Oathsworn Vampire for later when its graveyard recursion is relevant

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Angelic Cub 1/1 when the opponent had no untapped creatures to block and no mana available. This was a free point of damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Angelic Cub for 1 free damage, then play Plains and cast Taranika, Akroan Veteran in the post-combat main phase.

annotations.description: Played Forest instead of Treetop Village. Both allow casting Uktabi Orangutan this turn (2 Forest + 1 Swamp = 3 mana including G), but Treetop Village provides a creature-land for future turns, which is strictly more valuable than a basic Forest.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Treetop Village (enters tapped but still have 3 untapped mana to cast Uktabi Orangutan, and gain access to a 3/3 trample creature-land in future turns)

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Treetop Village in postcombat main phase. Since no mana can be used this turn anyway (everything is tapped, postcombat), the enters-tapped Treetop Village should be played now to maximize mana/options on future turns. Playing Forest now wastes the opportunity to 'hide' the tapped entry cost of Treetop Village.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest
annotations.betterLine: Play Treetop Village, which enters tapped but costs nothing this turn since it's postcombat. This preserves untapped land plays (Forest/Swamp) for future turns when immediate mana matters more.

annotations.description: Sonnet Trash failed to attack with Angelic Cub (a 2/2) when the opponent's only untapped creature is sick (Uktabi Orangutan just entered) and the Oathsworn Vampire is tapped. The opponent has no available blockers, so this is a free 2 damage. Missing this attack is a clear waste of tempo, though not game-losing since the life totals aren't critical yet.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and didn't declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Angelic Cub for 2 unblocked damage, bringing the opponent to 14 life.

annotations.description: Failed to block Oathsworn Vampire 2/2 with Taranika 3/3. Taranika would survive the block, kill the vampire (which has graveyard recursion potential), and save 2 life. The timeout/no response meant taking unnecessary damage and leaving the vampire alive.
annotations.actionTaken: No response — did not block, taking 2 damage from Oathsworn Vampire.
annotations.betterLine: Block Oathsworn Vampire with Taranika, Akroan Veteran. Taranika survives as a 3/1, kills the vampire, and saves 2 life with essentially no downside.

annotations.description: Activated Wily Bandar's indestructible ability for {2}{G} during combat, but Wily Bandar is not involved in combat and faces no threat. Opponent's lands are all tapped. This wastes 3 mana for zero benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Wily Bandar's indestructible ability giving it indestructible until end of turn while it wasn't in combat or under any threat.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority without activating the ability, saving the 3 mana for future use (e.g., contributing toward casting Hooting Mandrills next turn or activating Treetop Village).

annotations.description: Sonnet Trash failed to attack with Taranika, Akroan Veteran (3/3 vigilance) into an opponent with only a summoning-sick Wily Bandar 1/1 as a blocker. Taranika has vigilance so attacking has zero risk — she stays untapped. The opponent is at 16 life and can't block, so this is a free 3 damage. Missing this attack delays the clock significantly.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Taranika, Akroan Veteran for 3 unblockable damage (opponent's only creature is summoning sick). Taranika has vigilance so she remains untapped for defense.

annotations.description: Blocked Taranika 3/3 with Wily Bandar 1/1, trading away a creature that could have repeatedly blocked Taranika using its {2}{G} indestructible ability in future turns. At 16 life, taking 3 damage is very manageable, and preserving Wily Bandar as a recurring indestructible blocker is far more valuable.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Taranika with Wily Bandar, losing the 1/1 to save 3 life and deal 1 damage to Taranika.
annotations.betterLine: Don't block, take 3 damage (16 → 13), preserve Wily Bandar to use as a recurring indestructible blocker against Taranika in future turns when {2}{G} mana is available.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Hooting Mandrills before playing a land, resulting in a failed cast (rolled back by game engine). With 5 untapped lands and needing {5}{G} (reduced by Delve), the player should have played Swamp first to ensure 6 mana was available. Additionally, exiling Oathsworn Vampire to Delve is a real cost since it can be recast from graveyard. The sequencing error (spell before land) is a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Hooting Mandrills before playing a land, which was rolled back due to mana payment failure.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Marauding Blight-Priest ({2}{B}) and potentially also Hooting Mandrills with Delve (exiling Uktabi Orangutan and Wily Bandar but keeping Oathsworn Vampire). Or play Swamp, then cast Hooting Mandrills with proper Delve usage.

annotations.description: Cast Marauding Blight-Priest before playing a land drop. Standard sequencing dictates playing lands before spells to maximize available mana and information. While the land drop is still available postcombat, casting spells first risks forgetting the land drop and provides no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Marauding Blight-Priest before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (untapped) first, then cast Marauding Blight-Priest, preserving proper sequencing and maximizing mana availability

annotations.description: Activated Treetop Village while it was tapped and had summoning sickness, making it a 3/3 creature that cannot attack and is now vulnerable to creature removal for no benefit. The 2 mana spent accomplished nothing.

annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and move to combat/end step, preserving mana and not exposing Treetop Village to creature removal unnecessarily.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Taranika, Akroan Veteran (3/3 vigilance) into a completely open board where the opponent has no untapped creatures and all lands tapped. annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers, passing the combat phase.

annotations.description: Cast Hooting Mandrills before playing a land drop. Angelic Cub.oracle_text:
Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability for the first time each turn, put a +1/+1 counter on it.
As long as this creature has three or more +1/+1 counters on it, it has flying.

Blessed Sanctuary.oracle_text:
Prevent all noncombat damage that would be dealt to you and creatures you control.
Whenever a nontoken creature you control enters, create a 2/2 white Unicorn creature token.

Daybreak Charger.oracle_text: When this creature enters, target creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn.

Falconer Adept.oracle_text: Whenever this creature attacks, create a 1/1 white Bird creature token with flying that's tapped and attacking.

Hooting Mandrills.oracle_text:
Delve (Each card you exile from your graveyard while casting this spell pays for {1}.)
Trample

Infantry Veteran.oracle_text: {T}: Target attacking creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

Knight of the Tusk.oracle_text: Vigilance (Attacking doesn't cause this creature to tap.)

Marauding Blight-Priest.oracle_text: Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life.

Moment of Triumph.oracle_text: Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn. You gain 2 life.

Oathsworn Vampire.oracle_text:
This creature enters tapped.
You may cast this card from your graveyard if you gained life this turn.

Taranika, Akroan Veteran.oracle_text:
Vigilance
Whenever Taranika attacks, untap another target creature you control. Until end of turn, that creature has base power and toughness 4/4 and gains indestructible.

Thriving Grove.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color other than green.
{T}: Add {G} or one mana of the chosen color.

Thriving Heath.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color other than white.
{T}: Add {W} or one mana of the chosen color.

Treetop Village.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {G}.
{1}{G}: This land becomes a 3/3 green Ape creature with trample until end of turn. It's still a land. (It can deal excess combat damage to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.)

Uktabi Orangutan.oracle_text: When this creature enters, destroy target artifact.

Wily Bandar.oracle_text: {2}{G}: This creature gains indestructible until end of turn. (Damage and effects that say "destroy" don't destroy it.)
